findings.summary: records.rs already skips false booleans with `std::ops::Not::not`; a new `is_false` helper would duplicate that.
findings.evidence: records.rs lines 895, 1096 and 1421 use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]`. A Grep for `fn is_false` in records.rs found nothing. Fix: Use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]` on `reused`, matching the other fields, and drop the planned helper.

findings.summary: Criterion 3's Grep for the note text will match the new test fixture in verify.rs.
findings.evidence: The criterion 1 fixture sets the note to 'result reused from the CI run ...' inside verify.rs's test module, so a Grep over the whole file finds it. The plan's 'expect no match in judge()' admits this but gives no exact check. Fix: Either leave the note text out of the verify.rs fixture (the flag alone should make the test pass, which also proves judge() ignores the note), or limit the Grep to the judge() body, i.e. lines before `#[cfg(test)]`.

findings.summary: `runs_from_record` also builds records from `Source::Local` CI records; the plan does not say whether those get `reused: true`.
findings.evidence: checks.rs:237-241 matches `Source::Local => "local run"`. routing.rs:265 only uses records whose source is `Source::Ci`, so the case does not happen today. Fix: Say in the doc comment on `reused` that it marks any record reused from a recorded result (CI or local) for the same sha. That is still sound, because the sha must equal the candidate commit.

summary: The plan fixes the fault where it starts. In verify.rs, judge() at lines 318-325 only counts passing records whose exit code is 0. Records built from CI by checks.rs `runs_from_record` (lines 233-259) always have no exit code, so they never count. The plan adds `CheckRun.reused`, sets it where those records are built, and lets judge() count a passing record with no exit code only when the flag is set. It keeps the existing `candidate_tree == checks_tree` guard. I checked the commit-match argument and it holds: verification.rs:336-338 passes the candidate commit as both values (checks_tree is None for nested runs), and `runs_from_record` returns nothing when the sha differs (line 234). Skipped records stay excluded: `skipped_run` and the routing fallback at routing.rs:279-283 both build on `skipped_run`, so they inherit `reused: false`. A Grep for `CheckRun {` across crates returned exactly the literals the plan lists, so the compile-fix files beyond the stated deliverables are needed. Athena's six scope findings about them are reasonable, but these edits are forced by adding a field to the struct and are not scope creep. Criterion 1's test would fail on today's code. Criterion 2's tests guard against regressions (today's code already leaves those cases unmet, as the request's word "still" expects). Criterion 3 tests that the producer sets the flag, through `runs_from_record` and the routing reuse path. Criterion 4 tests that old records load and that a reused record round-trips. No athena.toml field and no external service is involved, and the work fits in one producer run. There are only minor issues: the plan proposes a new `is_false` helper where the file already uses `std::ops::Not::not`, and criterion 3's Grep for the note text will also match the new test fixture in verify.rs.
